How do StatefulSet pods with PersistentVolumeClaims behave when they are rescheduled to another node or another AZ, and why does this matter for EBS-backed volumes?
Compare BigQuery on-demand pricing with capacity pricing based on slots and editions. When does each one make sense?
How do BigQuery partitioning and clustering compare with Redshift sort keys and with Iceberg partitioning on S3?
Compare the GCP resource hierarchy of organization, folders and projects with AWS Organizations and accounts for isolating data teams and their billing.
Map these services across the two clouds and name one real difference for each pair: S3 and GCS, Kinesis and Pub/Sub, EMR and Dataproc, EKS and GKE.
A company runs its lake on AWS but its ML team wants to use BigQuery. What are the cost, latency, governance and egress concerns of this two-cloud setup?
Design a multi-account AWS strategy for a data platform. Which accounts would you create, what lives in each one, and which SCPs would you enforce across the organization?
Design a cost governance program for a data platform that spends 2 million USD a month. Cover budgets, tagging, showback or chargeback, anomaly alerts and who owns each action.
You are building a self-service data platform on AWS and Kubernetes for 20 product teams. What do you standardize as the golden path, and what do you leave to each team?

Set RPO and RTO targets for a data lake, a streaming pipeline and a warehouse. Which disaster recovery pattern (backup and restore, pilot light, warm standby or active-active) would you pick for each, and why?
A new law requires EU customer data to stay in the EU. How would you enforce data residency across S3, KMS keys, logs, backups, query engines and support access?
How would you plan the migration of 3 PB of data and 400 pipelines from an on-prem Hadoop cluster to AWS without a long freeze on new work?
Your platform team must choose between building on managed AWS services and running open-source engines on Kubernetes. Which criteria would you put in the design doc?
Explain supervised, unsupervised and self-supervised learning, with one data engineering example of each.
What is overfitting, how do you spot it from training and validation curves, and what are three ways to reduce it?
Why do we split data into train, validation and test sets, and what goes wrong if you tune hyperparameters on the test set?
Why is a random split wrong for time-series or event data, and how would you build a time-based split instead?
Give three concrete examples of label leakage in a churn model, and explain how a data engineer can prevent each one in the pipeline.
Define precision and recall. For a fraud model, which one would the business care about more, and why?
What does ROC AUC measure, and why can PR AUC be more useful when positives are only 0.1 percent of the data?
When would you report RMSE instead of MAE for a regression model, and how do outliers affect each one?
A fraud dataset has 1 positive per 1,000 rows. Compare downsampling, upsampling, class weights and threshold tuning, and explain what each does to the predicted probabilities.
What makes a good feature? Give examples of aggregations, ratios, time-since features and encodings for high-cardinality categories.
How would you choose a decision threshold for a classifier when false positives and false negatives have very different business costs?
What is the difference between data drift, concept drift and label drift? Give a real-world example of each.
Explain the bias-variance trade-off and how model complexity and the amount of training data affect each side.
What is model calibration, and why does it matter when a model's score is used as a probability by a downstream system?
What problem does a feature store solve, and what is the difference between its offline store and its online store?
What is point-in-time correctness, and how does an "as of" join stop future data from leaking into training rows?
Design a point-in-time join of 500 million labeled events against 200 feature tables in Spark. How do you keep it both correct and affordable?
What is training-serving skew? Give three ways it can happen even when both sides use the same feature names.
Would you share one feature code path between batch training and online serving, or log online features and train on those logs? Discuss the trade-offs.
How would you load batch features into an online store such as Redis or DynamoDB, and how do you handle TTLs and stale values?
How would you support a streaming feature such as "number of transactions in the last 5 minutes" with low serving latency and correct backfills?
Should your company build its own feature store or adopt one, such as Feast or a managed offering from a cloud or lakehouse vendor? What would you need to see to decide?
How do you version features and change a feature's definition without breaking models that are already in production?
What metadata should a feature registry hold so that a new team can find, trust and reuse a feature built by someone else?
What should experiment tracking record for each training run so that someone can reproduce the result six months later?
What is a model registry, and how do stages or aliases such as staging and production help control deployments?
Design a CI/CD pipeline for models. Which tests run on the data, on the training code and on the trained model before it can be promoted?
Compare batch scoring, online real-time inference and streaming inference, and give one use case for each.
How would you roll out a new model safely using shadow mode, canary traffic and A/B tests, and what would make you roll back?
What would you monitor for a model in production when the true labels only arrive 30 days later?
How do PSI or KL divergence work as drift metrics, and how do you avoid alert fatigue when you monitor hundreds of features?
How would you design a feedback loop that captures predictions, features and later outcomes so that models can be retrained and audited?
When should retraining run on a fixed schedule and when should drift or a drop in performance trigger it? What are the risks of fully automatic retraining?
Why should you log the exact model version and feature values used for each prediction, and what does that cost at 50,000 predictions per second?
What is a token, and why does the same text produce different token counts across models and languages?
What is a context window, and what are the cost and quality trade-offs of putting a very long document into the prompt?
What do temperature and top-p change during sampling, and what settings would you use for data extraction versus creative writing?
What is an embedding, and why can the cosine similarity between two embeddings stand in for "these texts mean similar things"?
Explain the difference between pretraining, fine-tuning and prompting. When would a data team choose fine-tuning over better prompts or RAG?
How would you get reliable structured JSON output from an LLM in a pipeline that extracts fields from 10 million documents?
Why do LLMs hallucinate, and which parts of a system design reduce hallucinations?
How would you estimate the monthly cost of an LLM feature from requests per day, input tokens, output tokens and cache hit rate? Which number usually dominates?
Walk through the main steps of a RAG pipeline, from document ingestion to the final answer, and say what can fail at each step.
Compare fixed-size, recursive, sentence-based and structure-aware chunking. How do chunk size and overlap affect retrieval quality?
How would you choose an embedding model for an internal search product? What would you test besides a public leaderboard score?
What is approximate nearest neighbor search, and why don't we run exact search over 100 million vectors?
Explain at a high level how an HNSW index works and what the `M`, `efConstruction` and `efSearch` parameters trade off.
Compare HNSW, IVF and product quantization indexes in memory use, build time, recall and the cost of updates.
What is hybrid search, and how would you combine BM25 keyword scores with vector scores, for example with reciprocal rank fusion?
What does a reranker such as a cross-encoder add after the first retrieval step, and what does it cost in latency?
How would you choose between a dedicated vector database, pgvector in Postgres, a search engine like OpenSearch, and vector search built into your lakehouse?
Source documents change every hour. How would you keep a vector index fresh, handle deletes, and avoid serving answers from removed documents?
How do you enforce document-level access control in RAG so a user never sees chunks they are not allowed to read? Compare filtering before retrieval with filtering after it.
What metadata would you store with each chunk, and how do metadata filters interact with recall in ANN search?
How would you evaluate a RAG system separately for retrieval quality and for answer quality? Name the metrics for each.
How would you build a golden evaluation set for a RAG assistant over company documents, and how many examples would you start with?
You must move 2 billion chunks to a new embedding model. How do you plan the re-embedding work, the cost and the cutover?
What are the trade-offs between storing raw chunk text in the vector database and storing only IDs that point to text in another store?
What is an LLM agent, and how is tool use (function calling) different from a single prompt and response?
What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP) at a concept level, and what problem does it solve when connecting models to tools and data?
You are asked to give an agent access to the company warehouse through a SQL tool. What guardrails would you add for safety, cost and correctness?
What is prompt injection, and how can text inside a retrieved document or a tool result try to take control of an agent?
Which guardrails would you put on inputs, on tool calls and on outputs for an agent that is allowed to write to production systems?
How do you write tool names, descriptions and input schemas so that a model picks the right tool and passes valid arguments?
What is an offline eval set for an LLM feature, and how is it different from a unit test?
What are the known pitfalls of LLM-as-judge, such as position bias, length bias and self-preference, and how do you check that a judge agrees with human raters?
How would you build an eval pipeline that runs on every prompt, model or retrieval change, and what should it store so results can be compared over time?
What should you log for every agent run so that you can debug a bad outcome later?
When is a multi-step agent the wrong design, and a fixed workflow with a few LLM calls the better choice?
How do you measure the cost and latency of an agent task that makes a different number of model and tool calls each time?
What is the KV cache, and why does GPU memory use grow with both batch size and sequence length?
Estimate the GPU memory needed to serve a 70 billion parameter model with 16-bit weights. What else besides the weights needs memory?
Explain static batching versus continuous batching for LLM inference, and why continuous batching raises throughput.
Explain the trade-off between latency and throughput in LLM serving. How do time to first token and tokens per second each change as batches get larger?
What is quantization, for example to 8-bit or 4-bit weights, and what do you gain and risk compared with 16-bit weights?
When would you use tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism or simply more replicas to serve a large model?
What are the prefill and decode phases of LLM inference, and why do they stress the GPU in different ways?
How would you autoscale LLM inference servers when a cold start means loading 100 GB of weights? Which signal would you scale on?
How would you calculate the cost per 1,000 requests for a self-hosted model, and when does self-hosting beat a hosted API?
Compare exact-match response caching, prompt prefix caching and semantic caching. What are the correctness risks of semantic caching?
What is PagedAttention, as used in vLLM, and which GPU memory problem does it solve?
Design a batch inference pipeline that runs an LLM over 500 million rows in the lake. How do you handle retries, rate limits, partial failures and cost?
What does speculative decoding do, and when does it reduce latency?
How would you plan GPU capacity so that a fixed pool is shared between training, batch inference and online serving across several teams?
Walk through a pipeline that turns raw web crawl data into a training-ready text dataset. What are the main stages?
Explain how MinHash with locality-sensitive hashing finds near-duplicate documents, and why exact hashing is not enough.
How would you run near-duplicate detection over 10 billion documents in Spark? Where are the shuffle and memory bottlenecks?
Which quality filters would you apply to web text, such as language ID, heuristic rules, classifier scores and perplexity, and how could each one bias the data?
How would you detect and remove PII such as emails, phone numbers and government IDs from a training corpus, and how do you measure the recall of the PII filter?
Where does tokenization fit in the data pipeline, and why should tokenized shards be versioned together with the tokenizer?
How would you make a training dataset fully reproducible, so that a run from three months ago can be rebuilt exactly? Which lineage would you record?
What is a data mixture, and how would you build tooling that lets researchers change mixture weights without re-running the whole pipeline?
How do you keep eval benchmark data out of the training data (decontamination), and how would you show that it worked?
Why do training data loaders prefer large sharded files in formats such as Parquet or WebDataset, and what goes wrong with millions of small files?
Your company wants an internal RAG assistant. Would you build it from open-source parts or buy a vendor product? Write down your decision criteria.
How should a data platform team support AI teams? Which parts do you offer as shared services, and which do you leave to each AI team?
How would you handle a user's data deletion request when their data may sit in training sets, embeddings, caches and fine-tuned models?
Design a governance process that decides which datasets can be used for training, covering licenses, consent, retention and approvals.
Should prompts and LLM responses be logged for quality work and debugging? How do you balance that with privacy and retention rules?
How would you decide whether to send company data to a third-party model API, use a private deployment, or self-host an open-weight model?

title: Debugging and production scenarios: 100 interview questions

qs.q: Your daily Spark job went from 1 hour to 3 hours overnight with no code change. Walk me through how you find the cause.
In the Spark UI, one stage has 199 tasks that finish in 30 seconds and 1 task that runs for 40 minutes. What do you check, and how do you fix it?
A join between a 2 TB events table and a 50 GB users table is skewed because 5 percent of events have a null or "unknown" user ID. Walk through three fixes and when you would pick each.
Executors keep failing with "Container killed by YARN for exceeding memory limits". What is actually running out of memory, and which settings and code changes do you try first?
The driver crashes with an OutOfMemoryError near the end of a job. Which code patterns commonly cause driver OOM, and how do you confirm which one it is?
The Spark UI shows very large "spill (disk)" numbers on a shuffle stage. What does that tell you, and what would you change?
A table written by your job now has 400,000 files averaging 200 KB each, and every downstream reader is slow. How did this happen, and how do you fix both the writer and the existing data?
A query that used to read one day of data now scans the whole table. How do you confirm that partition pruning stopped working, and what are the usual causes?
A few tasks in every stage run 5 times slower than the rest, on different keys each time. How do you tell a bad node from data skew, and when does speculative execution help?
After a Spark version upgrade, a job produces slightly different row counts. How do you find which behavior change caused it and prove which output is correct?
Adaptive query execution is turned on, but a skewed join is still slow. What would you check in the physical plan and in the AQE skew join settings?
A broadcast join that worked for a year now fails with a timeout or a driver OOM. What changed, and how do you make the job resilient to this kind of data growth?
A job fails with a FetchFailedException during a shuffle after running for 2 hours. What are the likely causes, and how do you narrow them down?
Your Spark compute costs doubled this quarter, but data volume grew only 20 percent. How do you find where the money went and which jobs to fix first?
Consumer lag on a critical topic grew from near zero to 2 hours over the morning. Walk me through how you decide whether the cause is the producer, the brokers or the consumer.
Downstream teams report duplicate records in a table fed by a Kafka consumer. List the ways duplicates can enter the pipeline and how you would find which one is happening.
Your consumer group rebalances every few minutes and throughput has dropped to almost nothing. What causes rebalance storms, and which settings and client changes stop them?
One partition of a topic gets 10 times the traffic of the others, and its consumer is always behind. How do you confirm a hot key, and what are your options?
After a broker failure, a team says some messages they got an acknowledgment for are gone. Which producer and topic settings make this possible, and how do you prove what happened?
Events for the same user arrive out of order in your consumer. What can cause this in a Kafka pipeline, and how do you design the consumer to cope with it?
Producers start getting timeout errors and request latency is high, but broker CPU looks normal. What else do you check?
A consumer committed offsets before writing its results and then crashed. How do you work out which records were lost, recover them, and stop this from happening again?
A new consumer group was deployed with `auto.offset.reset` set to `latest`, and the team says data is missing. Explain what happened and how you would backfill.
Disk usage on the brokers is growing fast and one broker is almost full. How do you find the cause, buy time safely, and fix the root problem?
A producer schema change caused every consumer to fail deserialization. How do you restore service quickly, and what process stops this next time?
Your streaming job's hourly counts are always about 3 percent lower than a batch recompute of the same hour. How do you find out whether late events are being dropped?
Someone set the watermark to 10 minutes, but mobile events often arrive 2 hours late. What symptoms would you see, and how would you pick a better watermark and handle the very late data?

A Structured Streaming job will not restart after a deploy and reports a checkpoint error. What could have corrupted or invalidated the checkpoint, and how do you recover without losing or duplicating data?
The state store of a streaming join grows every day until executors run out of memory. Which design mistakes cause unbounded state, and how do you fix them?
A Flink job's checkpoints started taking 10 minutes and are now timing out. What do you look at first?
After a code change, a streaming job restarts from its checkpoint but now produces wrong aggregates. Which kinds of changes are not safe to make with existing state?
A streaming job commits to a Delta or Iceberg table every 30 seconds, and readers of that table are getting slower each day. What is happening, and how do you fix it without adding much latency?
A streaming job's processing time per micro-batch keeps growing even though the input rate is flat. What are the possible causes?
A stream-stream join between orders and payments misses about 1 percent of matches. How do you find out whether the cause is the watermarks, the join keys or event timing?
An Airflow task has shown as "running" for 9 hours, but the worker has no process for it. What are the possible causes, and how do you clean it up safely?
Many Airflow tasks sit in "queued" and never start, although the workers look idle. What do you check?
A 30-day backfill finished, and now the target table has twice the expected rows for those days. How did that happen, and how do you repair the data?
Your team's pipelines are not idempotent, and every retry risks duplicates. How would you change the write patterns across 150 jobs, and in what order?
Every year when daylight saving time changes, one daily job either skips a day or runs twice. How do you find the bug and fix it for good?
A daily report shows a drop for "yesterday" every morning that fixes itself by noon. How do you tell whether this is a timezone bug, late-arriving data or a scheduling problem?
A job loaded only 60 percent of a day's files because the upstream drop was still in progress. How do you detect partial loads, and how do you redesign the pipeline to wait for complete data?
An upstream team re-sent a corrected file for last Tuesday. Walk through how you find and rerun every downstream job and table that is affected.
A task fails at random about once a week with a connection reset from the source database. How do you decide between adding retries, changing timeouts and fixing the source?
The Airflow scheduler is slow, DAG parsing takes minutes and tasks start late. What causes this, and what would you change in the DAG code and the deployment?
Two pipelines write to the same table and sometimes overwrite each other's partitions. How do you prove it is happening, and how do you redesign ownership?
The row count of a fact table fell 8 percent from yesterday, but no job failed. How do you find where rows are being silently dropped?
An inner join quietly drops rows because the dimension table is missing new keys. How would you catch this kind of silent row loss in the future?
An upstream service added a column and renamed another, and your pipeline still reports success. What breaks downstream, and how do you detect schema drift early?
The null rate of a key column jumped from 0.1 percent to 30 percent overnight. How do you trace where the nulls came from?
Revenue in a report is 4 times higher than expected after a new join was added. How do you prove that duplicate keys are exploding the join, and how do you fix it?
The Finance and Product dashboards show different numbers for "active users" last month. How do you find the reason, and how do you get the company to one number?
A data quality check fails every night, and the team has learned to ignore it. How do you fix both the checks and the habits around them?
A currency conversion bug inflated revenue for 3 weeks before anyone noticed. How do you find the affected rows and correct the historical tables and reports?
After a bad incident, leadership asks you to add data quality coverage to 2,000 tables. How do you catch real problems without flooding teams with false alerts?
A dedup step uses `row_number()` over a key ordered by timestamp, and on some days it keeps the wrong record. What is going wrong?
A CDC pipeline from Postgres still shows rows in the lake that were deleted in the source. How do you find where the deletes got lost?
An ML team finds that a feature table has been off by one day for six months. How do you size the impact, fix it, and tell the affected teams?
A dashboard query that ran in 5 seconds now takes 2 minutes. Walk through how you use the query plan and the query profile to find the cause.
Your warehouse bill jumped 60 percent in one week. How do you find which users, queries or jobs caused it?
Queries on a clustered table get slower every week as new data lands. Explain clustering decay, and how you would fix it and keep it fixed.
An analyst's query uses `SELECT DISTINCT` on top of a large join, runs very slowly and returns the wrong totals. What do you look for?
A query on an Iceberg table is slow because planning takes longer than execution. What do you check in the table metadata, and which maintenance fixes it?
A daily MERGE into a Delta table gets slower every day and now takes 3 hours. How do you find the reason and speed it up?
Two concurrent writers to a Delta or Iceberg table keep failing with commit conflicts. What causes this, and how would you change the write pattern?
Someone ran a DELETE without a WHERE clause on a production table. Walk through your recovery options in a lakehouse table and in a cloud warehouse.
Ad hoc queries from one team keep slowing down scheduled ELT jobs in a shared warehouse. How do you prove there is contention, and how do you isolate the workloads?
Old snapshots were expired on a table, and now a downstream incremental job fails. What happened, and how do you recover?
Spark executor pods on Kubernetes keep getting `OOMKilled` even though the JVM heap is well under its maximum. What is using the memory, and how do you fix the pod sizing?
A Python service in a pod has high latency, but dashboards show CPU usage well under its limit. How would you confirm CPU throttling and fix it?
Your Spark job writing to S3 starts failing with 503 Slow Down errors. Walk through the cause and the fixes on both the writer side and the key layout.
A Glue job that worked yesterday now fails with Access Denied on an S3 read. Walk through how you find which policy is denying the request.
The NAT gateway bill tripled this month. How do you find which workloads are sending traffic through it, and what do you change?
Pods for a new deployment stay in Pending for 20 minutes. What are the possible reasons, and which commands and events do you check?
A deployment goes into CrashLoopBackOff right after a config change. How do you find the cause and roll back safely?
At peak hours your pipelines start failing with throttling errors from AWS APIs such as the Glue Data Catalog. How do you find which calls are throttled and reduce them?
A long EMR job on Spot capacity keeps failing in its last hour when Spot nodes are reclaimed. How do you make it finish reliably without moving everything to On-Demand?
After every rolling deploy, about 2 percent of requests to a service fail with connection errors for a minute. How do you find the cause?
A Terraform plan for production wants to destroy and recreate a database. How do you investigate before anyone approves the apply?
After the weekly re-index, users say the RAG assistant's answers got worse. How do you find out what changed in the data, the chunking or the index?
Right after a deploy, vector search starts returning nearly random results, but no errors are logged. What would you check first, and how would you stop this from happening again?
P99 latency of your LLM endpoint jumped from 2 seconds to 12 seconds while average latency barely moved. How do you investigate?
An inference server crashes with CUDA out of memory, but only on some requests. Which request properties do you look at, and which server settings would you change?
A fine-tuning job fails with GPU out of memory at step 4,000 but not at step 1. What could make memory grow during training, and how do you find it?
The eval score of your LLM feature dropped 6 points after a prompt change that "should not matter". How do you tell a real regression from eval noise, and what do you do next?
An agent sometimes loops, calling the same tool 40 times until it hits the step limit. How do you debug it and stop it from happening?
A RAG assistant showed a user a snippet from a document they had no access to. How do you contain the incident and find the gap in the access control path?
Your LLM API bill doubled in a week while user traffic stayed flat. How do you find the cause?
A batch LLM job over 50 million rows is 80 percent done and keeps failing on rate limits and timeouts. How do you finish it without reprocessing rows or paying twice?
The answer quality of a hosted model seems to have changed even though nothing changed on your side. How do you confirm it, and how do you protect your product from this in the future?
A fraud model's precision fell by half in production right after its feature pipeline moved to a new engine. How do you prove or rule out training-serving skew?
You are the incident commander for a data outage that broke the executive revenue dashboard on the morning of an earnings call. Walk through your first 30 minutes.
How do you decide the severity of a data incident? Give an example of a SEV1 and a SEV3 for a data platform.
Write the first status update you would send to stakeholders when you know the data is wrong but not yet why. What do you include, and what do you leave out?
During an incident, when do you stop looking for the root cause and instead roll back or switch to a known-good snapshot?
Walk through a blameless postmortem for a pipeline that published wrong numbers for 3 days. What makes the action items actually get done?
The same type of incident has happened three times this quarter in different teams. How do you drive a fix across teams you do not manage?
After a fix, how do you verify that the data is correct again, and how do you decide when to tell users they can trust the dashboard?
After a string of incidents, you are asked to set data SLOs for freshness, completeness and correctness on critical tables. How do you pick them, and how do they change on-call and alerting?
You are paged at 3 a.m. for a failed job that feeds a report used at 9 a.m. How do you triage, and how do you decide whether to fix it now or wait?
Tell me about the worst data incident you led: what happened, what you did in the first hour, and what you changed afterward so it could not happen again.
Design clickstream ingestion for 1 million events a second, with events arriving up to 3 days late from offline mobile clients.
Design a nightly batch load of 2,000 tables from 30 OLTP databases into a warehouse, where the load must finish by 6 a.m. and some tables have no last-updated column.
Design change data capture from 500 sharded MySQL databases into a lakehouse, keeping tables less than 5 minutes behind the source while schema changes happen without warning.
Design CDC from a single 20 TB Postgres database into Kafka and then Iceberg, where the initial snapshot must not slow down production queries.
Design hourly ingestion from 200 third-party SaaS APIs such as Salesforce, Stripe and Zendesk, each with different rate limits, pagination and auth.
Design an IoT telemetry pipeline for 50 million devices sending readings every 10 seconds over flaky cellular links, where devices buffer data offline and replay it out of order.
Design a company-wide logging platform that takes in 20 PB of application logs a month from 10,000 services, with 7 days of fast search and 1 year of cheap cold storage.
Design an event pipeline with exactly-once delivery from a payments service to the ledger warehouse at 50,000 events a second, running across two regions.
Design a schema registry and event contract process for 300 Kafka topics owned by 60 teams, so a breaking change is caught before it reaches production.
Design a mobile and web event SDK plus collection backend for 2 billion daily active users, with client-side batching, sampling and a kill switch for a bad event without an app release.
Design a dead letter queue and replay system for a stream of 300,000 events a second, where 0.1% of events fail parsing and must be fixed and replayed within a day.
Design a real-time sales dashboard for a retail chain with 3,000 stores and 20,000 checkout events a second, with numbers less than 10 seconds old.
Design ad impression and click aggregation for 10 billion impressions a day, where advertisers are billed from the counts and any double counting costs real money.
Design click fraud filtering inside an ad aggregation pipeline at 2 million events a second, where invalid clicks found up to 48 hours later must be removed from advertiser bills.
Design a top-K trending hashtags service over 500,000 posts a second, with 1-minute, 1-hour and 24-hour windows.
Design an A/B testing platform that runs 5,000 experiments at once across 1 billion users and computes 200 metrics per experiment every day with confidence intervals.
Design assignment and exposure logging for an experimentation platform with 300 million users, where users switch devices and log in partway through an experiment.
Design a company metrics platform (a semantic layer) where 1,000 metrics are defined once and give the same answer in dashboards, notebooks, experiments and executive reports.
Design a real-time count of unique viewers for 100,000 concurrent live streams, where an approximate answer within 2% error is acceptable.

Design a streaming join of order, payment and delivery events for a food delivery app at 50,000 events a second, where any stream can be late or missing and order status must be correct within 1 minute.
Design a real-time OLAP store for an internal product analytics tool where 5,000 analysts slice 100 billion rows by 40 dimensions and expect answers in under a second.
Design a daily Spark job that joins a 50 TB events table with a 2 TB users table, where 1% of users create 40% of events and skew keeps crashing the job.
Design a backfill system that can safely recompute 2 years of daily partitions for 300 downstream tables after a bug fix, without breaking dashboards people use during the day.
Design incremental processing for a 100 TB fact table that gets late updates to any date in the last 90 days, so you never rebuild the whole table.
Design the recovery and reprocessing plan after a bad deploy wrote wrong revenue numbers for 6 hours into both the real-time store and the warehouse.
Design workflow orchestration for 20,000 daily tasks across 80 teams, with SLAs, retries, cross-team dependencies and clear ownership when a task fails at 3 a.m.
Design a batch and streaming setup for session metrics where the real-time number and the next-day batch number must match within 0.5%.
Design a sessionization job for 30 billion page views a day, where a session ends after 30 minutes of inactivity and sessions can cross midnight and time zones.
Design the data model and pipeline for a hotel bookings warehouse with 2 million bookings a day, where bookings can be changed, cancelled and partly refunded weeks later.
Design the warehouse for a ride-sharing app with 30 million trips a day that supports driver pay, surge pricing analysis and city-level dashboards.
Design a payments warehouse that reconciles 100 million transactions a day against bank settlement files, with many currencies and chargebacks that arrive up to 120 days later.
Design the data model for streaming playback analytics that tracks start time, rebuffering and watch time for 200 million daily viewers across TVs, phones and browsers.
Design an e-commerce warehouse for orders, returns and inventory across 20 countries, where prices and categories change over time and reports must use the value at the time of sale.
Design a social feed analytics warehouse that shows how ranking changes affect time spent, for 3 billion users and 100 billion feed impressions a day.
Design the data model and pipeline behind a creator earnings dashboard that shows daily earnings from ads, subscriptions and tips, matching finance payouts to the cent.
Design the data model and pipeline behind a "Year in Review" feature that gives 500 million users a personal summary, computed in 2 weeks and launched on a single day.
Design the data model and pipeline behind a seller dashboard for a marketplace with 5 million sellers, showing sales, fees and payouts updated every 15 minutes.
Design a customer 360 table that links web cookies, app device IDs, emails and phone numbers for 800 million people, where identity links can be added and removed later.
Design the data model for a subscription business that reports MRR, churn and cohort retention, where plans upgrade, downgrade, pause and get refunded mid-cycle.
Design a lakehouse platform on Iceberg for 50 PB of data and 3,000 users, covering table format, catalog, compaction, snapshot expiry and access control.
Design the fix for a streaming job that writes to an Iceberg table every minute and has created 40 million small files in one month.
Design a migration of 30,000 Hive tables to Iceberg with zero downtime for 2,000 daily jobs and no change in query results.
Design the move of a 10 PB on-prem Hadoop platform to the cloud over 12 months, with both systems running in parallel and numbers that must match before cutover.
Design the table layout (partitioning, clustering and sort order) for a 5 PB events table that is queried both by date range and by user ID.
Design a zero-downtime move from a self-managed Kafka cluster handling 3 GB a second to a managed streaming service, with no lost or duplicated events.
Design upserts and deletes into a 200 TB lakehouse table from a CDC stream of 100,000 changes a second, and choose between copy-on-write and merge-on-read.
Design a multi-engine lakehouse where Spark, Trino, Flink and a Python notebook service all read and write the same tables safely, with one catalog and one set of permissions.
Design a data quality platform that runs checks on 20,000 tables daily and stops bad data from reaching 500 downstream dashboards, without so many alerts that people ignore them.
Design anomaly detection on row counts and key metrics for 5,000 daily pipelines, where weekends, holidays and launches look like anomalies but are not.
Design column-level lineage for a warehouse with 100,000 tables built from SQL, Spark and dbt, so an engineer can see every dashboard affected by a column change.
Design a data catalog and search for 200,000 datasets, where a user must find the one trusted revenue table among 40 tables with similar names.
Design a GDPR deletion platform that removes one user's data from 3,000 tables, logs, backups and ML training sets within 30 days, with proof that it happened.
Design a PII detection and tagging system that scans 10 PB of existing data plus every new column each day, then applies masking and access rules automatically.
Design freshness and SLA tracking for 1,000 critical tables, so a late upstream job alerts the owners of every affected downstream table.
Design a consent system where the privacy choices of 1 billion users (ads, analytics, AI training) are enforced in every pipeline that reads their data.
Design the debugging tools and runbook for when daily revenue drops 8% overnight and you must decide within 1 hour if it is a real change or a pipeline bug.
Design a multi-tenant Spark platform on Kubernetes for 150 teams sharing 20,000 cores, with fair scheduling, quotas and protection from one team's runaway job.
Design autoscaling for a Flink job on Kubernetes whose traffic swings from 50,000 to 800,000 events a second during a daily peak.
Design a cost attribution system that shows each team its monthly compute, storage and query spend on a data platform that costs 40 million dollars a year.
Design a cost-aware query platform that cuts warehouse spend by 30% without slowing down the 500 most important dashboards.
Design a storage tiering policy for 80 PB in S3 where 90% of reads touch the last 30 days of data but audits need 7 years.
Design an interactive SQL service in the style of Trino for 3,000 analysts with 400 concurrent queries at peak, where no single query can starve the rest.
Design cross-region disaster recovery for a warehouse and its 3,000 pipelines, with a recovery time of 4 hours and less than 15 minutes of lost data.
Design a feature store serving 2,000 features to 50 models, with online lookups in less than 10 ms at 1 million requests a second and the same values used in offline training.
Design point-in-time correct training data for a churn model with 100 million users, so no feature leaks information from after the prediction date.
Design real-time fraud features for card payments at 20,000 transactions a second, such as spend per card and per merchant in the last 5 minutes, with a decision in less than 50 ms.
Design the feature pipeline for a recommendation system that needs user embeddings refreshed daily and recent click history refreshed within 1 minute.
Design the training data pipeline for a feed ranking model that logs 50 billion impressions a day, with features captured at serving time and labels that arrive up to 7 days later.
Design a labeling data pipeline where 5,000 human labelers tag 2 million images a week, with quality checks, consensus voting and versioned datasets.
Design model monitoring that detects feature drift and prediction drift for 300 production models, and links each alert to the upstream table that changed.
Design an embedding platform for 5 billion items that rebuilds all embeddings when the model changes and keeps old and new versions live during the switch.
Design dataset versioning so any model trained in the last 2 years can be retrained on exactly the same data.

secs.name: AI engineering: RAG, search and evaluation

qs.q: Design RAG over 10 million company documents from Google Drive, Confluence and Slack, where every answer must respect the asking employee's document permissions.
Design the ingestion and re-indexing pipeline for a RAG system where 200,000 documents change every day and deleted documents must disappear from answers within 15 minutes.
Design a search indexing pipeline for a marketplace with 500 million listings, where price and stock changes must show up in search within 30 seconds.
Design an evaluation platform for an AI assistant that runs 50,000 test prompts on every model or prompt change and reports quality, safety and cost regressions within 2 hours.
Design the logging and feedback pipeline for a chatbot with 20 million conversations a day, capturing ratings, edits and follow-up questions for later training.
Design an LLM-as-judge pipeline that scores 1 million model outputs a day, with a way to measure how often the judge agrees with human raters.
Design hybrid keyword and vector search over 100 million support tickets, with filters by product, date and customer tier.

secs.name: AI infrastructure: inference, training data and agents

qs.q: Design an LLM inference platform serving 5 models to 300 internal teams at 100,000 requests a minute, with per-team quotas, priority tiers and token-level billing.
Design the pipeline that turns 5 PB of raw web crawl into a deduplicated, filtered and PII-scrubbed pre-training dataset, with every filter step reproducible.
Design agent infrastructure for 1 million agent runs a day that call tools and keep memory across sessions, where every step is logged so a failed run can be replayed.
Design usage and token metering for an AI API with 50,000 customers, where bills must be exact and customers see their usage within 1 minute.
Design checkpoint storage and data loading for a 10,000-GPU training cluster, where a data loader stall wastes thousands of GPU hours.
Design a GPU usage analytics pipeline that shows each research team its GPU hours, idle time and failed jobs across 20,000 GPUs, updated every 5 minutes.
Your company has 40 teams each building their own pipelines with different definitions of active user. Design the platform and the plan to fix it.
Leadership wants the data platform bill cut from 60 million to 40 million dollars a year within 12 months without hurting product teams. Design the plan, the tooling and how you will measure success.
After two acquisitions your company runs Redshift, Snowflake and BigQuery side by side. Design the target architecture and a 2-year consolidation plan.
Data incidents reach executives twice a month and nobody knows who owns the broken tables. Design the ownership model, tooling and on-call process that fixes this.
The company launches an AI assistant in 6 months and 15 product teams need shared data for RAG, fine-tuning and evaluation. Design the platform and the roadmap.
A new privacy law means you must show where every piece of personal data lives and who used it, across 8,000 pipelines, within 9 months. Design the system and the rollout.
Your 25 ML teams have each built their own feature pipelines and training data jobs with heavy duplication. Design a shared ML data platform and how you will get teams to adopt it.
The batch warehouse is 24 hours behind and product teams now want everything in real time. Design the strategy, including what should and should not become real time.
A data platform team of 30 engineers supports 2,000 internal users and is drowning in support tickets. Design a self-serve platform and a plan to cut tickets in half.
Your company runs 400 streaming jobs with no shared standards, and last month one bad job took down a shared Kafka cluster. Design the guardrails, the platform and the migration plan.
Your product will let 10,000 enterprise customers bring their own data for analytics and AI features, with strict tenant isolation. Design the platform.
The in-house pipeline framework is 8 years old, runs 70% of all jobs and only 2 people understand it. Design the plan to replace or modernize it without freezing new work.
The company is expanding into 5 new countries with data residency rules. Design the data architecture so a new region can be added in weeks, not quarters.
Researchers, analysts and product engineers want different things from the data platform and keep escalating to leadership. Design the operating model, platform tiers and roadmap.
You are the first staff data engineer at a 200-person AI startup with no data platform. Design what you build in the first 6, 12 and 24 months and what you choose not to build.
Tell me about a time you convinced another team to change their roadmap to support your project, without any authority over them.
Tell me about a time you got five or more teams to adopt a standard, tool or platform they did not ask for. How did you win over the first team?
Describe a time you changed a more senior engineer's mind on a technical decision. What evidence did you bring?
Tell me about a time you built support for a big proposal before the formal review, so the decision was mostly made before the meeting.
Tell me about a time you had to influence a director or VP outside your management chain. What did you do differently for that audience?
Tell me about a time your idea was rejected at first. What did you change, and did it happen in the end?
Describe a time you led engineers from several teams, none of them reporting to you, toward a shared goal. How did you keep them committed?
Tell me about a time a design doc or strategy doc you wrote changed how a whole org worked.

secs.name: Technical direction, strategy and cross-team alignment

qs.q: Tell me about a time you set the technical direction for a data platform for the next 2 to 3 years. How did you decide what to bet on?
Walk me through a technical strategy you wrote. Who read it, what changed because of it, and what did you get wrong?
Tell me about a project you led that needed work from three or more teams. How did you keep the plan in sync?
Tell me about a time two teams were building overlapping systems. How did you find out and what did you do?
Describe a time you got engineering, product and data science to agree on one definition of a key metric.
Tell me about a time you picked a new technology for your team. How did you evaluate it and limit the risk?
Tell me about a time you stopped a popular project or technology choice because you believed it was the wrong direction.
Tell me about a cross-team project that slipped badly. How did you get it back on track, and what did you change for next time?
Tell me about a time you strongly disagreed with your manager. How did you raise it and what happened?
Tell me about a conflict with a peer engineer over a design. How did you resolve it?
Tell me about a conflict between your team and another team over who owns a system or dataset. How was it settled?
Tell me about a time a product manager kept changing requirements late in a project. How did you handle it?
Tell me about a time a senior stakeholder asked for a number or dashboard you knew would mislead people. What did you do?
Tell me about a time you disagreed with a decision but committed to it fully. How did you show that commitment?
Tell me about a time you committed to a decision you disagreed with and it later proved wrong. What did you do then?
Tell me about a time you had to settle a conflict between two strong engineers on different teams.
Tell me about a time you were the one who was wrong in a disagreement. How did you realize it and what did you do next?
Tell me about your biggest technical mistake. What was the impact and what did you change afterwards?
Tell me about a time bad data reached a dashboard, model or customer. How did you find out and what did you do in the first hour?
Tell me about the worst production incident you led. How did you coordinate people, update leadership and decide when to roll back?
Tell me about a postmortem you ran where the root cause was another team's change. How did you keep it blameless and still get fixes done?
Tell me about a time you were on call and had to make a hard call at night with very little information.
Tell me about a time you cut the on-call load or incident rate for a whole org. What were the numbers before and after?
Tell me about a project you led that failed or was cancelled. What would you do differently?
Tell me about a time you missed something in a code or design review that later caused a problem.
Tell me about a time you were given a vague goal with no clear requirements. How did you turn it into a plan?
Tell me about a time nobody owned an important system or dataset. How did you find an owner or take it on yourself?
Tell me about a time you had three important projects and people for only one. How did you decide, and who did you tell?
Tell me about a time you said no to a request from a senior stakeholder. How did you say it?
Tell me about a time you paused or killed your own team's project so a more important one could move faster.
Tell me about a technical decision you made with incomplete data. How did you limit the damage if you were wrong?
Tell me about a build-versus-buy decision for a data platform component. What drove the decision, and was it right?
Tell me about a time you chose speed of delivery over long-term quality. How did you manage the cost later?
Tell me about a time the problem you were asked to solve turned out to be the wrong problem.
Tell me about a time priorities changed in the middle of your project. How did you decide what to keep, cut or hand off?
Tell me about a decision you made that was very hard to reverse. How did you decide it was worth it, and who did you involve?

secs.name: Simplification, raising the bar and growing others

qs.q: Tell me about a time you simplified a complex system that many teams depended on. What did you remove and how did you prove it was safe?
Tell me about a time you paid down tech debt. How did you get time for it and how did you measure the result?
Tell me about a time you made the case to leadership for a large tech debt or reliability investment. What numbers did you use?
Tell me about a time you pushed back in a code review that others had already approved. What was the issue and how did the author react?
Tell me about a standard you introduced, such as testing, data contracts or design reviews, that raised the quality bar across several teams.
Tell me about a time you argued against hiring someone others liked, or for someone others doubted. What happened?
Tell me about someone you mentored. What did they struggle with, what did you do, and where are they now?
Tell me about a time you helped a senior engineer grow into a tech lead or staff role. What did you deliberately hand over to them?
Tell me about a time you gave hard feedback to a peer. How did they take it?
Tell me about a time you raised the technical level of a whole team, not just one person.

secs.name: Delivery, business impact and data-driven decisions

qs.q: Tell me about a time you delivered a project on a tight deadline. What did you cut and how did you decide?
Tell me about the project with the biggest business impact in your career. Give the numbers in revenue, cost or users.
Tell me about a time you cut the cost or runtime of a data system. What were the before and after numbers, and how did you measure them?
Tell me about a time data you produced changed a product or business decision. What was the decision and what happened?
Tell me about a time the data told a different story from what leadership believed. How did you present it?
Tell me about a time you set success metrics for a platform before building it. Did you hit them?
Tell me about a time you saw a project was going to miss its deadline. When did you tell people and what options did you give them?

secs.name: Ethics, privacy, security and research partnerships

qs.q: Tell me about a time you found sensitive data where it should not be, such as personal data in logs. What did you do?
Tell me about a time you pushed back on a use of data that was legal but felt wrong for users.
Tell me about a time you balanced a security or privacy requirement against a team's need to move fast.
Tell me about a time you worked closely with researchers or scientists. How did you handle their changing needs and different way of working?
Tell me about a time a research or ML team needed data infrastructure that did not exist yet. How did you decide what to build first?
Tell me about a time you had to explain an infrastructure limit to a research team that wanted something faster or bigger. How did you find a way forward?
Why do you want a staff role, and what do you think changes day to day from senior to staff?
Why this company, and why now? What do you know about its data and AI infrastructure problems?
Why are you leaving your current job?
Where do you want to be in 5 years, on a deep technical track or in management, and why?
What is the largest scope you have owned so far, and what larger scope do you want to own in this role?

secs.name: Deep dive into your most complex project

qs.q: Walk me through the most complex data system you have designed or led. Start with the problem and the scale.
On that project, why did you choose your design over the two strongest alternatives?
If you rebuilt that system today, what would you change and why?

What exactly did you personally do on that project, as opposed to your team?
What broke in production after that system launched, and what did it teach you about the design?
How did that project change the way other teams worked, and how do you know?
Tell me about a time you dug into raw data or code and found that a summary everyone trusted was wrong.
Tell me about a time you started from what the customer needed and worked backwards, and it changed the technical plan.
Tell me about a time you built a small tool or automation that saved other engineers hours every week.

Tell me about a time you acted quickly without all the information because waiting would have cost more.
Tell me about a time you delivered more with fewer people or less budget than you asked for.
Tell me about a time you thought much bigger than the original ask. Did it pay off?
Tell me about a time you had to learn a new area fast because a project needed it.
Tell me about a time you refused to lower the quality bar even though it delayed a launch.
Tell me about a time you lost the trust of a team or stakeholder. How did you earn it back?
Tell me about a time you fixed a problem that was not your job because nobody else was going to.
